title: Identity Platform — External Error Contract (v1, FROZEN)
description: The complete, stable set of externally observable authentication/authorization/OAuth error codes. Generated to match, and drift-guarded against, src/contracts/identity-error.contract.ts and src/modules/resource-server/errors/resource-server-error.ts / src/modules/oauth/errors/oauth-token-error.ts (docs/API_SECURITY_CONTRACT_FREEZE.md). No new code introduced by this document — it restates what Phase 2D.4-2D.9 already implemented and tested.

bearer_token_errors.description: IdentityBearerErrorCode — errors from any route protected by ExternalBearerAuthGuard / ResourceAuthorizationGuard.

codes.meaning: Malformed request shape (e.g. ambiguous multiple Authorization headers).
Token missing, malformed, expired, wrong signature/issuer/audience, unknown kid, or an ID Token presented as a bearer token — never further distinguished externally.
Token valid, but lacks a required OAuth scope.
Token valid and scoped, but denied at the product-authorization layer (missing/suspended/revoked entitlement, no policy registered, product policy denied, provider error).

token_endpoint_errors.description: IdentityTokenEndpointErrorCode — POST /oauth/token and GET /oauth/authorize errors (RFC 6749 §5.2, unchanged).

codes.meaning: Client not authorized for the requested grant type.
grant_type is not authorization_code or client_credentials.
Requested scope not allowed for this Application.
Requested audience not allowed for this Application, or a wildcard/forbidden value.
ServiceAccount/tenant-grant/entitlement eligibility check failed — a single generic code for every reason (non-enumeration).
Authorization code unknown/expired/already-consumed/malformed, or presented with the wrong client/redirect_uri/PKCE verifier — a single generic code for every reason (non-enumeration).

rate_limit_error.description: RateLimitExceededException (Phase 2D.9) — shares the same generic HttpException wire shape.

compatibility_policy.adding_a_new_code: non-breaking — products must treat an unrecognized code as a generic denial, never crash
compatibility_policy.removing_or_renaming_a_code: BREAKING — requires a new major contract version
compatibility_policy.changing_an_http_status_for_an_existing_: BREAKING — requires a new major contract version
compatibility_policy.enumeration_guarantee: no code, ever, distinguishes 'client does not exist' / 'tenant does not exist' / 'service account does not exist' / 'product not entitled' from any other reason mapping to the same code — verified by the existing Phase 2D.4-2D.9 test suites, re-verified this phase with zero change
